title: Recent Advances in Multimodal Dissolved Oxygen Forecasting in Aquaculture: A Review
content:
ABSTRACT

Dissolved oxygen (DO) affects respiration, feeding, growth and welfare in aquaculture. DO forecasting can provide early warning of hypoxia and inform aeration decisions. Most aquaculture forecasts use time series from fixed monitoring locations; these describe temporal variation but contain limited information on biological oxygen demand, management activity and spatial distribution. This review traces the transition from single-point time-series prediction to multimodal DO forecasting. Environmental and operational variables capture external forcing and interventions associated with DO dynamics. Biological, behavioural and physiological observations provide information on oxygen demand and animal responses, whereas spatial and hydroacoustic observations characterise fish distribution and biomass across locations and depths. The review covers spatiotemporal alignment, missing-value reconstruction, multimodal fusion, and temporal, spatiotemporal, multimodal and hybrid forecasting models. Applications include hypoxia warning, DO-field forecasting and reconstruction, and forecast-informed oxygen management. Across the literature, DO and physicochemical measurements form the observational basis and are supplemented by biological, spatial and operational information selected for each forecasting task. Asynchronous observations, missing data and variable sensor reliability complicate multimodal fusion, while differing forecast horizons and evaluation settings affect comparisons across studies. Field deployment is further affected by sensor drift, biofouling and differences among production sites. Priorities for future research include quality-aware and mechanism–data fusion, transferable models evaluated under comparable horizons and event definitions, and prospective studies linking prediction error to warning lead time, spatial risk and management outcomes. In brief, this review aims to help researchers and practitioners understand multimodal DO forecasting and its potential to guide oxygen management in aquaculture.
